cards.explanation: The answer is only the Father. Jesus says, “No one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father.” That's a short list, friends, and it has exactly one name on it. So I quit trying to guess a date. I just keep my ovens warm and my apron on.

The answer is Noah. Jesus says, “As it was in the days of Noah, so will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.” Out of every picture He could pick, He points back to the days before the flood, when people carried on right up to the day Noah entered the ark. So when He talks about His coming, that's the picture He hands us.

The answer is eating and drinking and marrying. Jesus says people were “eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, up to the day Noah entered the ark.” That's everyday life, friends. Meals, weddings, the normal rhythm of things. Jesus puts it right up to the day Noah went in.

The answer is False. The people before the flood did not see it coming. Jesus says, “they were oblivious until the flood came and swept them all away.” Oblivious means they were unaware of it. It's a heavy picture, so let it sit a moment. Then Jesus says, “So will it be at the coming of the Son of Man.”

The answer is one taken and one left. Jesus says, “Two men will be in the field: one will be taken and the other left.” Same field, two different outcomes. He keeps the picture short and plain. I think the point is that being in the same place doesn't mean the same outcome.

The answer is watch. Jesus says, “Therefore keep watch, because you do not know the day on which your Lord will come.” Nobody puts a batch in the oven and then wanders off to rearrange the pantry. You stay close, you stay alert, and you keep an eye on the timer. Jesus asks His disciples to do that same watching.

The answer is that he would have kept the thief from breaking in. Jesus says that if the homeowner had known, “he would have kept watch and would not have let his house be broken into.” So the key is knowing the hour and staying alert. The trouble is that nobody gets that hour handed to them. That's the point of the story.

The answer is ready. Jesus says, “For this reason, you also must be ready, because the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect.” He takes the homeowner picture and points it at His disciples. The reason comes right after the word: an hour you do not expect. Ready is the word, friends, and it's the same word my ovens live by.

The answer is that he is blessed. Jesus says, “Blessed is that servant whose master finds him doing so when he returns.” Doing what? Giving the others their food at the proper time. It's steady, faithful work, and the master finds him right in the middle of it.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, he will put him in charge of all his possessions.” The servant was trusted with the household, and he's trusted with even more. The master finds him doing his job and puts him over everything he owns. Faithful work gets noticed.

The answer is “My master will be away a long time.” Jesus says the wicked servant “says in his heart, ‘My master will be away a long time.’” So he expects his master to be gone a long while. Then watch what he does, friends, because Jesus is about to tell us.

The answer is False. The wicked servant does not keep giving the others their food. Jesus says he “begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with drunkards.” Giving the others their food at the proper time is what the faithful servant does (Matthew 24:45). He's the one the master finds doing so when he returns (Matthew 24:46).

The answer is on a day the servant does not expect. Jesus says, “The master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not anticipate.” The servant had told himself his master would be away a long time. Then the master comes on a day he doesn't expect. That's the whole surprise.
